sentences.text:
By this petition, the petitioners seek review of the judgment dated 31.01.2023 passed in WP(C)
No.2183/2019, whereby this Court has dismissed the writ petition.
2.

The judgment is sought to be reviewed on the ground that this Court has not considered certain vital aspects of the matter and has, thus, landed in an error apparent on the face of record in coming to the conclusion that the petitioners were entitled to the compensation for shamilat deh land on pro-rata basis.

3. Having heard Mr. S.A.Naik, learned counsel appearing for the applicants and perused the material on record, we are of the view that all aspects of the case highlighted by the learned counsel appearing before us were duly considered and determined in the light of settled legal position.

4. The short grievance that was projected by the learned counsel for the petitioners in the writ petition was that they were in possession of shamilat land and, therefore, were entitled to compensation to the exclusion of other villagers/shareholders in the shamilat land.
The petitioners had called in question the recommendations of the committee dated 04.09.2013 insofar as these relate to payment of compensation for shamilat land under Rule 5.

This Court took note of the Ghulam Nabi Wani And Another vs State Of J&K And Others on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35463392/

sentences.text:
factual background of the case and found that the Director Industries and Commerce, Kashmir vide his communication dated 04.01.2013 placed an indent with the Collector, Land Acquisition,
Pulwama for acquisition of land measuring 416 Kanals, 19 marlas and 3 Sirsai ["subject land"] for establishment of Industrial Estate at Khrew.
The said land was notified for acquisition by the Collector by issuing notification under Section 4(1) of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, 1990 ["the Act"].

It also came to fore that out of the subject land, land measuring 239 kanals and 13  marlas was proprietary in nature, while as, rest of the land measuring 177 Kanals, 5 marlas and 7  Sirsai was partible shamilat land classified as shamilat under Section 5.
Pursuant to private negotiations, rate of Rs.5.00 lac per kanal was determined to be paid to the owners/interested persons by way of compensation for the acquired land.
The compensation for the proprietary land was immediately disbursed to the rightful claimants, i.e. recorded owners as per the revenue record.
With regard to partible shamilat land, the matter was taken up by the Collector Land Acquisition with Tehsildar, Pampore to prepare a pro rata report indicating the share of each land holder.
On the basis of the report submitted by the Tehsildar, compensation at the rate determined by the Private Negotiation Committee was paid to the rightful claimants.

4. The grievance of the petitioners in the writ petition was that they being in possession of the shamilat land were entitled to receive compensation for the land in their possession irrespective of their share in the shamilat land on pro rata basis.
The petitioners laid their claim on a sale deed executed by a Kashmiri Pandit in their favour transferring his share in their favour.

The Collector,
Land Acquisition, refused to accede to the request of the petitioners to disburse them the compensation for the entire Shamilat land under their occupation and instead disbursed the compensation on pro rata basis and not on the basis of actual possession.

This aspect was considered by this Court and having found that the petitioners were not entitled to compensation for the entire shamilat land under their possession rejected the plea of the petitioners in this regard.
The writ petition was, thus, found to be without any merit and was, accordingly, dismissed.

5. Today also, Mr. S.A.Naik, learned counsel appearing for the review petitioners, reiterated the same submissions and as a matter of fact, wants us to sit in appeal against the judgment which we have passed in WP(C) No.2183/2019 on 31.01.2023.

We are afraid that scope of review is not, too,
extensive to permit this Court to revisit its decision on merits.
Mr. Naik despite his vehemence could not point out any error apparent on the face of record, which would persuade us to review a well reasoned judgment passed by us.
6. For the foregoing reasons, we find no merit in this review petition.

The same is, accordingly,
dismissed.
(M A Chowdhary) (Sanjeev Kumar)
Judge Judge Jammu
